text_blocks.snippet: The Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, often referred to as the FSO, is a piece of UK legislation that consolidates previous fire safety laws into a single framework. It places the responsibility for fire safety on the "responsible person" within various premises, requiring them to assess fire risks and implement necessary precautions. This includes ensuring safe escape routes, providing adequate fire safety training, and maintaining fire safety equipment.

list.title: Consolidation of Fire Safety Law:
list.snippet: The FSO replaced numerous previous fire safety regulations, including the Fire Precautions Act 1971.

list.title: "Responsible Person":
list.snippet: This is the individual who has control over the premises, such as the employer or occupier, and is accountable for fire safety.

list.title: Fire Risk Assessment:
list.snippet: The responsible person must conduct a suitable and sufficient fire risk assessment to identify potential hazards and implement appropriate fire safety measures.

list.title: General Fire Precautions:
list.snippet: This includes ensuring safe escape routes, fire detection and alarm systems, fire-fighting equipment, and clear signage.

list.title: Training and Information:
list.snippet: Employees must receive adequate fire safety training, including induction and refresher courses.

list.title: Maintenance of Equipment:
list.snippet: Fire safety equipment, including fire detection and alarm systems, must be properly maintained and kept in good working order.

list.title: Application:
list.snippet: The FSO applies to most non-domestic premises in England and Wales, including workplaces, venues, and some residential properties. It does not generally apply to private dwellings.

list.title: Enforcement:
list.snippet: Enforcement is typically carried out by local fire and rescue authorities, who can issue enforcement notices and prosecute those who fail to comply with the FSO.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, the FSO aims to ensure that premises are safe from fire and that people can escape safely in the event of a fire.
